q: Cash from operations differs from funds from operations mainly because cash from operations is arrived at after adjusting funds from operations for:

options.A: Depreciation charged during the year only
options.B: Profit or loss on sale of fixed assets only
options.C: Changes in current assets other than cash and in current liabilities, such as debtors, stock and creditors
options.D: Income-tax paid during the year only

q: Net working capital represents the portion of current assets that is financed by:

options.A: Long-term sources of funds
options.B: Trade creditors only
options.C: Short-term bank borrowings only
options.D: Current liabilities

q: Other things being equal, an enterprise with a longer production or manufacturing cycle will require:

options.A: Less working capital than an enterprise with a shorter cycle
options.B: No working capital at all
options.C: More working capital, because funds remain locked up for a longer period in work-in-progress
options.D: The same working capital irrespective of the cycle length

q: Which of the following will tend to reduce the working capital requirement of an enterprise?

options.A: Prompt collection from debtors and faster turnover of inventory
options.B: A liberal credit policy allowing customers longer time to pay
options.C: Longer storage of raw materials before use in production
options.D: A large seasonal peak in production and sales

q: Current assets of an enterprise are Rs 9,50,000 and its current liabilities are Rs 4,50,000. Its net working capital is:
An enterprise has stock of Rs 2,00,000, debtors of Rs 1,50,000 and cash of Rs 50,000 as its only current assets. Its gross working capital is:

Raw materials are held for 40 days, the production process takes 20 days, finished goods are held for 25 days and debtors are collected in 50 days. Creditors allow 35 days' credit. The length of the operating cycle is:

options.A: 135 days
options.B: 100 days
options.C: 85 days
options.D: 115 days

q: The annual operating cost of an enterprise is Rs 36,50,000, reckoning a year of 365 days. Its operating cycle is 50 days. On the operating-cycle method, the working capital required is:
A public utility undertaking generally needs relatively less working capital mainly because:

options.A: It renders services largely for cash and does not carry large inventories of finished goods
options.B: It incurs no operating expenses
options.C: It purchases all its materials only for cash
options.D: Its production cycle is the longest among all industries

q: PERT was originally developed in 1958 for:

options.A: Scheduling the construction of a chemical plant by DuPont
options.B: Preparing the annual railway budget
options.C: The Polaris missile programme of the US Navy
options.D: Controlling inventory in a manufacturing concern

q: CPM was originally developed by DuPont primarily for:

options.A: Appraising the return on a new railway line
options.B: Fixing freight rates for goods traffic
options.C: Analysing variances in standard costing
options.D: Scheduling and controlling construction and plant maintenance projects where activity times are fairly predictable

q: The correct distinction between PERT and CPM as regards orientation is:

options.A: PERT is activity-oriented and CPM is event-oriented
options.B: Both PERT and CPM are event-oriented
options.C: PERT is event-oriented and CPM is activity-oriented
options.D: Both PERT and CPM are activity-oriented

q: In PERT, an activity has an optimistic time of 8 days, a most likely time of 14 days and a pessimistic time of 26 days. Its expected time is:

options.A: 14 days
options.B: 15 days
options.C: 16 days
options.D: 18 days

q: In PERT, an activity has an optimistic time of 4 days, a most likely time of 13 days and a pessimistic time of 16 days. Its expected time is:

options.A: 12 days
options.B: 11 days
options.C: 13 days
options.D: 10 days

q: In PERT, the optimistic time of an activity is 7 days and the pessimistic time is 19 days. The standard deviation of the activity time, computed as (TP - TO) / 6, is:

options.A: 2 days
options.B: 4 days
options.C: 6 days
options.D: 12 days

q: As compared to PERT, CPM places greater emphasis on:

options.A: The probability of completing the project by a given date
options.B: The use of three time estimates for each activity
options.C: The sequencing of events in a research project
options.D: Optimising project cost by balancing direct cost against project time, that is, the cost-time trade-off

q: A key limitation of sensitivity analysis in project appraisal is that it:

options.A: Cannot be used with the Discounted Cash Flow technique
options.B: Always requires the cost of capital as an input
options.C: Varies one variable at a time assuming the other variables remain unchanged, thus ignoring inter-relationships between variables and the probability of the change occurring
options.D: Considers only the payback period of the project

q: In project appraisal, sensitivity analysis mainly helps management to:

options.A: Guarantee the projected rate of return of the project
options.B: Identify the critical variables to whose changes the project's return is most sensitive, so that they can be estimated carefully and monitored closely
options.C: Eliminate all risk from the project
options.D: Fix the discount rate to be used in appraisal

q: A controllable variance is a variance:

options.A: Which arises wholly from external factors beyond anyone's control
options.B: Which is always favourable to the enterprise
options.C: For which a specific manager or department can be held responsible, because it arises from factors within their control
options.D: Which is too small to be investigated

q: The fixed overhead capacity variance arises due to the difference between:

options.A: Budgeted fixed overheads and actual fixed overheads incurred
options.B: Budgeted hours of work and actual hours worked, valued at the standard fixed overhead rate
options.C: Standard output and actual output in units only
options.D: Budgeted variable overheads and actual variable overheads

q: A favourable material price variance should not automatically be regarded as good performance because it may have been achieved by:

options.A: Negotiating a genuine and lasting reduction in price
options.B: Purchasing materials in economic order quantities
options.C: Paying suppliers promptly to earn cash discount
options.D: Buying inferior quality material, which may cause an adverse usage variance and production problems

q: A finance lease is distinguished from an operating lease in that a finance lease:

options.A: Transfers substantially all the risks and rewards of ownership to the lessee and generally covers a major part of the asset's economic life
options.B: Is always cancellable by the lessee at short notice without penalty
options.C: Covers only a small fraction of the asset's economic life
options.D: Leaves all risks of ownership with the lessor throughout

q: The lease rentals payable by Indian Railways to IRFC for rolling stock leased to it essentially comprise:

options.A: Only the dividend on the capital-at-charge
options.B: Recovery of the principal, that is the capital component, and interest on the funds raised for that stock
options.C: Only the maintenance cost of the rolling stock
options.D: Only the depreciation charge of the rolling stock

q: Extra Budgetary Resources through Institutional Finance, EBR(IF), are raised mainly to finance:

options.A: Remunerative projects and acquisition of rolling stock that can service the debt from their earnings
options.B: Day-to-day establishment and pension payments
options.C: Routine repairs and maintenance of track
options.D: Only unremunerative passenger amenity works

q: Lease financing enables the Railways to acquire rolling stock:

options.A: Free of cost from the leasing company
options.B: Without paying any rental during the lease period
options.C: Without meeting the entire capital cost upfront from budgetary resources, the payment being spread as lease rentals over the life of the asset
options.D: Without any liability being recorded for the lease rentals

q: In PPP terminology, DBFOT stands for:

options.A: Design, Build, Fund, Own and Transfer
options.B: Develop, Build, Finance, Own and Transfer
options.C: Design, Bid, Finance, Operate and Terminate
options.D: Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer

q: Under the Viability Gap Funding scheme for PPP projects, the Central Government may provide up to 20% of the total project cost and the sponsoring authority up to a further 20%. The maximum total Viability Gap Funding is therefore:

options.A: 20% of the total project cost
options.B: 25% of the total project cost
options.C: 30% of the total project cost
options.D: 40% of the total project cost

q: In a PPP project, the concession agreement is the agreement between:

options.A: The SPV and its lenders only
options.B: The main contractor and its sub-contractors
options.C: The government authority granting the concession and the SPV or concessionaire, giving it the right to build and operate the facility for the concession period
options.D: The SPV and the users of the facility

q: A basic principle of risk allocation in PPP projects is that each risk should be allocated to:

options.A: The party best able to manage and bear that risk at the least cost
options.B: The government in every case
options.C: The private partner in every case
options.D: The lenders financing the project in every case

q: In IRPSM, proposals for new works in the Works Programme are initiated and processed by:

options.A: Contractors executing railway works
options.B: Field units, divisions and zonal railways, which feed the proposals online for examination and prioritisation
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General
options.D: Passengers and freight customers

q: IRPSM assists in capital budgeting and appraisal mainly by providing:

options.A: A system for fixing tariffs and freight rates
options.B: A system for collecting cash earnings at stations
options.C: A common online platform for examination, finance scrutiny, prioritisation within the budget ceiling and inclusion of proposals in the Pink Book
options.D: A system for conducting the statutory audit of works

q: After a work is sanctioned, IRPSM is used for:

options.A: Monitoring its physical and financial progress, expenditure and milestones against the sanction
options.B: Fixing the pay of staff posted on the work
options.C: Selling surplus materials arising from the work
options.D: Preparing the personal claims of officers supervising the work

q: In traffic costing, the cost of a traffic service is broadly analysed into:

options.A: Fixed costs and period costs only
options.B: Terminal costs and line-haul or movement costs
options.C: Fuel costs and staff costs only
options.D: Capital costs and dividend payable on capital

q: Specific Energy Consumption for electric traction in railway costing is generally expressed as energy consumed per:

options.A: 100 Net Tonne Kilometres
options.B: 1000 Passenger Kilometres
options.C: Wagon day
options.D: 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres

q: Pricing a traffic service strictly on its fully distributed cost may lead to loss of otherwise remunerative traffic because:

options.A: A service that does not cover its fully distributed cost may still make a positive contribution if its earnings exceed the incremental or marginal cost of carrying it
options.B: Fully distributed cost includes no share of overheads at all
options.C: Marginal cost is always higher than fully distributed cost
options.D: Fully distributed cost is based only on fuel consumption

q: A cost is classified as a direct cost of a particular job when it:

options.A: Is incurred for the factory as a whole
options.B: Remains fixed in total at all levels of output
options.C: Can be economically identified with and traced to that job in full
options.D: Is apportioned to the job on the basis of floor area

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Product costs are inventoried and carried forward as part of the value of stock until the goods are sold.
2. Period costs are charged in full against the revenue of the period in which they are incurred.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The salary of a factory manager who supervises several jobs, none of which can claim his time exclusively, is treated in the cost of an individual job as:

options.A: An indirect labour cost recovered through factory overheads
options.B: A direct labour cost of the largest job
options.C: A direct expense of every job in full
options.D: A selling overhead of the job

q: Discretionary (managed) fixed costs are distinguished from committed fixed costs in that discretionary fixed costs:

options.A: Arise from owning plant and long-term leases
options.B: Cannot be altered even over several years
options.C: Vary in direct proportion to output
options.D: Arise from periodic management decisions, such as research and publicity outlays, and can be curtailed without immediately impairing capacity

q: In a cost sheet, administration overheads are added after arriving at:

options.A: Prime cost
options.B: Works (factory) cost, to arrive at the cost of production
options.C: Cost of sales, to arrive at the selling price
options.D: Direct material cost only

q: When output rises within the existing capacity, the behaviour of costs is best stated as:

options.A: Total variable cost rises, variable cost per unit stays constant, and fixed cost per unit falls

options.D: Total fixed cost rises in proportion to output

options.A: 200 units

options.C: 400 units
options.D: 800 units

q: The minimum stock level of a material is fixed primarily to ensure that:

options.A: The maximum possible quantity is always held in stores

options.C: The re-order quantity is fully consumed before the next order
options.D: Obsolete stock can be disposed of quickly

q: In a period of steadily rising material prices, valuing issues under FIFO, as compared to the weighted average method, will generally result in:

options.A: A higher charge to production and a lower value of closing stock
options.B: No difference in either charge or stock value
options.C: Issues priced at the latest prices in both methods
options.D: A lower charge to production and a higher value of closing stock, because the earliest (cheaper) lots are charged out first

q: A worker is allowed 12 hours for a job and completes it in 9 hours at a wage rate of Rs 60 per hour. His total earnings under the Halsey premium bonus plan (50% of time saved) are:

options.A: Rs 630

q: The Rowan premium bonus plan differs from the Halsey plan in that under the Rowan plan the bonus is:

options.B: Over-absorbed by Rs 12,000

options.A: Carrying it forward indefinitely as an asset
options.B: Adding it to the cost of the next year's production only

options.A: Rs 8,000 (Favourable)

options.A: Rs 7,500 (Favourable)

options.A: 1 only

q: In sensitivity analysis, the 'switching value' of a project variable is:

q: Two mutually exclusive machines have different economic lives. The Net Present Value of one machine is Rs 1,10,000 and the cumulative present value (annuity) factor for its life at the cost of capital is 2.5. Its Equivalent Annual Annuity (equivalent annual benefit) is:
A new machine costs Rs 5,60,000. The old machine it will replace can be sold immediately for Rs 90,000. The net (incremental) initial cash outlay on the replacement is:
In a machine replacement decision, the book value of the existing machine is generally irrelevant to the decision (except for any tax or disposal effect) because it is:

options.A: Always equal to its current realisable value
options.B: A sunk cost representing capital already spent, which cannot be recovered by either alternative
options.C: A future cash outflow under both alternatives
options.D: Included in the price of the new machine

q: In appraising a new project, an amount already spent on a preliminary survey for that very project in an earlier year should be treated as:

options.A: A cash outflow of the project in its first year
options.B: A part of the initial investment of the project
options.C: A sunk cost, excluded from the project's cash flows, since it will remain spent whether or not the project is now accepted
options.D: A deduction from the project's earnings in the final year

q: The earnings projected in the financial justification of a new railway line rest principally on traffic projections, under which the traffic expected on the new line is made up of:

options.A: Only the traffic already moving on the existing lines of the railway
options.B: Only the traffic carried in the first year of operation
options.C: Originating traffic, traffic diverted from existing routes or modes, and newly generated (developed) traffic
options.D: Only the coaching traffic expected on the line
